html:
The last and harshest Roman persecution of Christians, begun in 303 by Diocletian and his co-rulers of the Tetrarchy. Galerius is often seen as its driving force.

A series of edicts ordered churches pulled down and scriptures burned, stripped Christians of legal rights, jailed clergy, and finally demanded that everyone sacrifice to the gods. How hard it hit depended on the ruler. In Gaul and Britain, under Constantius, only the first edict was applied. In the east it went on for years, with many executions.

Galerius, dying, issued an edict of toleration in 311. In 313 Constantine and Licinius confirmed it in the Edict of Milan. Within a few decades Christianity went from hunted faith to the state religion. The church remembered this time as the age of martyrs, and quarrels over those who had handed over scriptures led to the Donatist split in Africa.
sum: The last and harshest Roman persecution of Christians, begun in 303 by Diocletian and his co-rulers of the Tetrarchy. Galerius is often seen as its driving force.
